course.title: Restaurant Management
course.tagline: Run a small restaurant: menus, staff, costs and customers, without the chaos.

days.title: What Does a Restaurant Manager Do?
days.goal: Know the job of a restaurant manager.

video.title: How to Open a Restaurant or Hotel (Step-by-Step) | Complete Business Guide for Beginners 2026

steps: A manager runs the restaurant day to day.
The job covers money, staff, food, and customers.
A good manager plans ahead, not just reacts.
You need to know your numbers: sales, costs, and profit.
You need to lead people, not just give orders.
days.task: Write down the five jobs of a manager: money, staff, food, customers, and planning.
days.challenge: Visit a restaurant and watch how the manager works.

quiz.q: What does a restaurant manager do?
options: Run the restaurant day to day: money, staff, food, and customers
quiz.explain: A manager runs everything: money, staff, food, and customers.

quiz.q: Why must a manager plan ahead?
options: Planning stops problems before they happen
quiz.explain: Planning ahead stops stock-outs, staff gaps, and unhappy customers.

quiz.q: What numbers must a manager know?
quiz.explain: Sales, costs, and profit tell you if the restaurant is healthy.

days.title: Your Restaurant Idea: Concept and Customers
days.goal: Pick a restaurant idea and know your customers.

video.title: How to EASILY Use Restaurant SOPs (Step-by-Step Guide) | DAY 69

steps: A concept is the idea of your restaurant: what food, what style, what price.
Pick food you can cook well and people want to buy.
Know your customers: who they are and what they can pay.
Look at other restaurants near you. What do they do well?
Write your concept in one short paragraph.
days.task: Write your restaurant concept in one paragraph.
days.challenge: List three restaurants near you and what they do well.

options: The idea: what food, what style, what price
quiz.explain: A concept is the whole idea of the restaurant.

options: So you cook food they want at a price they can pay
quiz.explain: Knowing customers helps you pick the right food and price.

options: To learn what works and find your own gap
quiz.explain: Other restaurants show you what works and where you can be different.

days.title: Business Plan: The Simple Version
days.goal: Write a simple business plan for a small restaurant.

video.title: Toast POS System Tutorial for Beginners

steps: A business plan is a written plan for your restaurant.
It covers your idea, your customers, your menu, and your money.
List your start-up costs: rent, equipment, stock, and licences.
Work out how much you must sell each day to cover costs.
Keep it short and clear. One or two pages is enough to start.
days.task: Write a one-page business plan for a small restaurant.
days.challenge: List your start-up costs with real prices.

options: A written plan for your restaurant: idea, customers, menu, and money
quiz.explain: A business plan writes down your idea, customers, menu, and money.

options: Money you spend once to open: rent, equipment, stock, licences
quiz.explain: Start-up costs are the one-time costs of opening.

quiz.q: Why work out daily sales needed?
options: So you know if the restaurant can pay its bills
quiz.explain: Knowing the sales you need tells you if the plan can work.

days.title: Food Cost: The Most Important Number
days.goal: Work out food cost and food cost percentage.

video.title: Restaurant — Recipe, Food Cost and Kitchen Stock

steps: Food cost is what the ingredients for a dish cost you.
Food cost percentage is food cost divided by the selling price, times 100.
Example: a dish costs ₦1,000 to make and sells for ₦3,000. Food cost is 33 percent.
Most restaurants aim for 28 to 35 percent.
If food cost is too high, you lose money on every plate.
days.task: Cost one dish and work out its food cost percentage.
days.challenge: Cost three dishes from a menu and compare.

options: What the ingredients for a dish cost you
quiz.explain: Food cost is the cost of the ingredients in one dish.

quiz.q: How do you work out food cost percentage?
options: Food cost divided by selling price, times 100
quiz.explain: Food cost divided by the selling price, times 100, gives the percentage.

quiz.q: What is a good food cost percentage?
quiz.explain: Most restaurants aim for 28 to 35 percent.

days.title: Menu Pricing: Set Prices That Make Money
days.goal: Price a menu using food cost.

video.title: Recipe for Restaurant Profits

steps: Price equals food cost divided by the food cost percentage you want.
Example: food cost ₦1,000, target 30 percent. Price is ₦1,000 divided by 0.30, which is about ₦3,333.
Round to a clean price, like ₦3,500.
Check what other restaurants charge for the same dish.
Do not price too low. Low prices can mean no profit.
days.task: Price five dishes using the food cost method.
days.challenge: Compare your prices with a restaurant near you.

quiz.q: How do you set a price from food cost?
options: Food cost divided by the food cost percentage you want
quiz.explain: Price equals food cost divided by your target food cost percentage.

quiz.q: Why round to a clean price?
options: Clean prices are easier for customers and staff
quiz.explain: Clean prices like ₦3,500 are easy to remember and pay.

options: Low prices can mean no profit
quiz.explain: Prices that are too low may not cover your costs.

days.title: Menu Design: What Sells
days.goal: Design a menu that helps customers choose and helps you earn.

video.title: Restaurant Menu Pricing: How to Increase Profit

steps: Keep the menu short. Ten to fifteen dishes are enough.
Put your most profitable dishes where eyes go first: the top and the middle.
Use clear names and short descriptions.
Mark your best sellers with a star or a note.
Remove dishes that never sell. They waste stock and time.
days.task: Design a menu of 12 dishes.
days.challenge: Mark your three most profitable dishes on it.

quiz.q: How many dishes should a small menu have?
quiz.explain: Ten to fifteen dishes are enough for a small restaurant.

quiz.q: Where do eyes go first on a menu?
quiz.explain: Eyes go to the top and middle first. Put profitable dishes there.

quiz.q: Why remove dishes that never sell?
quiz.explain: Slow dishes tie up stock and kitchen time.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Restaurant Plan
days.goal: Write a full plan for a small restaurant.

video.title: Restaurant Menu Pricing Without Guessing

steps: Write your concept in one paragraph.
Design a menu of 12 dishes with prices.
Cost three dishes and work out their food cost percentage.
Write your start-up costs and daily sales target.
Show the plan to a friend and ask for honest feedback.
days.task: Write a full one-page restaurant plan.
days.challenge: Cost three dishes and price the menu.

quiz.q: What should a restaurant plan include?
options: Concept, menu, prices, costs, and sales target
quiz.explain: A plan covers concept, menu, prices, costs, and sales target.

quiz.q: Why cost dishes before you open?
options: So you know your prices make a profit
quiz.explain: Costing before you open stops you selling at a loss.

quiz.q: Why show the plan to a friend?
options: Fresh eyes spot problems you missed
quiz.explain: A friend can spot gaps in your plan.

project.title: Write a Restaurant Plan
project.brief: Write a concept, a 12-dish menu with prices, costs, and a sales target.
checks: Concept written in one paragraph
Menu of 12 dishes designed
Three dishes costed with food cost percentage
Prices set using the food cost method
Start-up costs and daily sales target written
Plan shown to a friend for feedback

days.title: SOPs: Write Down How Things Are Done
days.goal: Write simple SOPs for your restaurant.

video.title: How to Price Menu Items

steps: SOP means Standard Operating Procedure. It is a written way of doing a job.
Write one SOP for opening the restaurant each morning.
Write one SOP for closing at night.
Write one SOP for taking an order.
Keep SOPs short: steps in order, in plain words.
days.task: Write an SOP for opening your restaurant.
days.challenge: Write an SOP for taking an order.

options: A written way of doing a job, step by step
quiz.explain: An SOP is a written set of steps for doing a job the same way every time.

options: So every staff member does the job the same good way
quiz.explain: SOPs keep quality the same, even when staff change.

quiz.q: How long should an SOP be?
options: Short: steps in order, in plain words
quiz.explain: Short, plain SOPs are easy to read and follow.

days.title: Hiring Staff: Find Good People
days.goal: Hire staff who fit your restaurant.

video.title: Your Complete Guide To Restaurant Inventory Management

steps: List the jobs you need: cook, server, cleaner, cashier.
Write a short job description for each one.
Hire for attitude first. Skills can be taught.
Check references. Ask past employers how the person worked.
Start new staff on a trial. Watch how they work with customers.
days.task: Write job descriptions for three roles.
days.challenge: Practise asking interview questions with a friend.

quiz.q: What should you hire for first?
quiz.explain: A good attitude matters most. Skills can be taught on the job.

options: Past employers tell you how the person really worked
quiz.explain: References show if a person is honest and hard-working.

quiz.q: Why start new staff on a trial?
options: So you can see how they work before you commit
quiz.explain: A trial shows how a person really works with customers.

days.title: Training Staff: Teach the Basics
days.goal: Train new staff simply and clearly.

video.title: An Easy Guide to Restaurant Operations Management

steps: Show, then let them try, then watch them do it alone.
Train on the menu: staff must know every dish.
Train on service: greet, take orders, serve, check back.
Train on safety: hand washing, food storage, and cleaning.
Give feedback kindly and quickly. Praise good work.
days.task: Write a one-day training plan for a new server.
days.challenge: Practise training a friend to take an order.

quiz.q: What is the best way to train?
options: Show, let them try, then watch them do it alone
quiz.explain: Show, try, then do alone is the fastest way to learn a job.

quiz.q: Why must staff know the menu?
options: So they can answer customer questions
quiz.explain: Staff who know the menu can help customers choose and sell more.

options: So staff can fix mistakes while they remember
quiz.explain: Quick feedback helps staff learn fast.

days.title: Staff Scheduling: The Right People at the Right Time
days.goal: Make a weekly staff schedule.

video.title: How to Open a Restaurant or Hotel (Step-by-Step) | Complete Business Guide for Beginners 2026

steps: Look at busy times: lunch and dinner are busiest.
Put more staff on busy shifts and fewer on quiet shifts.
Give staff at least one day off each week.
Keep a backup list for when someone is sick.
Share the schedule early so staff can plan.
days.task: Make a weekly schedule for a small restaurant.
days.challenge: Work out the labour cost for the week.

quiz.explain: Lunch and dinner are the busiest times.

quiz.q: Why put more staff on busy shifts?
quiz.explain: More staff on busy shifts means fast service and happy customers.

options: So staff can plan their week
quiz.explain: Early schedules help staff plan and reduce no-shows.

days.title: Inventory: Know What You Have
days.goal: Track stock so you never run out or waste food.

video.title: How to EASILY Use Restaurant SOPs (Step-by-Step Guide) | DAY 69

steps: Inventory means all the food and supplies you have.
Count stock once a week, at the same time.
Write down what you have, what you used, and what you need.
Use FIFO: First In, First Out. Use old stock first.
Order before you run out, not after.
days.task: Count the stock in your kitchen and write it down.
days.challenge: Make a simple stock list with reorder levels.

options: All the food and supplies you have
quiz.explain: Inventory is everything you have in stock: food and supplies.

options: First in, first out: use old stock first
quiz.explain: FIFO means use the oldest stock first so nothing goes bad.

options: So you know what you have and what to order
quiz.explain: Weekly counts stop stock-outs and waste.

days.title: POS Systems: Take Orders and Payments
days.goal: Use a POS system to run orders and payments.

video.title: Toast POS System Tutorial for Beginners

steps: POS means Point of Sale. It is the system that takes orders and payments.
A POS records what was sold, so you know your best sellers.
It tracks stock as dishes are sold.
Train staff to use it well. Mistakes cost money.
Check the daily sales report every night.
days.task: Watch a POS tutorial and list its main features.
days.challenge: Practise entering an order on paper as if on a POS.

options: The system that takes orders and payments
quiz.explain: A POS is the system for orders, payments, and sales records.

quiz.q: Why does a POS track stock?
options: So you know what is running low
quiz.explain: A POS that tracks stock tells you what to reorder.

quiz.q: Why check the daily sales report?
options: So you know what sold and what you earned
quiz.explain: Daily reports show what sold, what earned, and what to fix.

days.title: Week 2 Project: Run a Pop-Up Restaurant
days.goal: Run a small pop-up restaurant for a day.

video.title: Restaurant — Recipe, Food Cost and Kitchen Stock

steps: Pick a menu of 5 dishes with prices.
Write SOPs for opening, serving, and closing.
Make a staff schedule for the day.
Cook and serve to friends or family as customers.
Count your sales, costs, and profit at the end.
days.task: Run a pop-up restaurant for a day.
days.challenge: Work out your sales, costs, and profit.

options: It tests your plan with low risk
quiz.explain: A pop-up tests your menu, prices, and systems before you open for real.

quiz.q: What should you count at the end?
quiz.explain: Sales, costs, and profit tell you if the day made money.

quiz.q: Why write SOPs for a pop-up?
options: So helpers do the job the same good way
quiz.explain: SOPs keep service smooth even with helpers.

project.title: Run a Pop-Up Restaurant
project.brief: Run a one-day pop-up with a menu, SOPs, schedule, and sales count.
checks: Menu of 5 dishes with prices
SOPs written for opening, serving, closing
Staff schedule made for the day
Food cooked and served to customers
Sales, costs, and profit counted
Feedback collected from customers

days.title: Customer Service: The Basics
days.goal: Serve customers so they return.

video.title: Recipe for Restaurant Profits

steps: Greet every customer with a smile within 30 seconds.
Listen fully. Do not interrupt.
Repeat the order back to get it right.
Check back within 2 minutes of serving food.
Thank customers and invite them back.
days.task: Practise serving a friend, step by step.
days.challenge: Ask your friend what made the service feel good.

quiz.q: How fast should you greet a customer?
quiz.explain: A fast greeting makes customers feel welcome.

quiz.q: Why check back after serving food?
quiz.explain: Checking back early lets you fix problems before customers get angry.
Repeating the order stops mistakes.

days.title: Handling Complaints
days.goal: Handle unhappy customers calmly and well.

video.title: Restaurant Menu Pricing: How to Increase Profit

steps: Listen first. Let the customer finish speaking.
Say sorry, even if it is not your fault.
Ask what would make it right.
Fix it fast: replace the dish, offer a discount, or give a free drink.
Thank them for telling you. Complaints help you improve.
days.task: Practise handling a complaint with a friend playing the customer.
days.challenge: Write a short guide for staff on handling complaints.

quiz.q: What is the first step with a complaint?
quiz.explain: Listening first shows respect and helps you understand the problem.

options: It shows you care about the customer
quiz.explain: An apology calms the customer and shows you care.

quiz.q: Why thank a customer for complaining?
options: Complaints show you what to fix
quiz.explain: Complaints point out problems you can fix.

days.title: Daily Operations: Open to Close
days.goal: Run a restaurant day from open to close.

video.title: Restaurant Menu Pricing Without Guessing

steps: Morning: check stock, prep food, clean the dining room.
Before service: hold a short team meeting. Share the specials.
During service: watch the floor, help where needed, check food quality.
After service: count cash, check the POS report, clean up.
Write a short note on what went well and what to fix.
days.task: Write a daily operations checklist.
days.challenge: Run a practice day using your checklist.

options: A short team meeting to share specials and jobs
quiz.explain: A short meeting gets the team ready for service.

quiz.q: What should a manager do during service?
options: Watch the floor, help, and check food quality
quiz.explain: A manager on the floor spots problems early.

quiz.q: Why write a note at the end of the day?
options: So you remember what to fix tomorrow
quiz.explain: Daily notes help you improve a little every day.

days.title: Food Safety in a Restaurant
days.goal: Keep a restaurant kitchen safe.

video.title: How to Price Menu Items

steps: Wash hands often. Wear clean clothes and a hair cover.
Keep raw meat away from cooked food.
Keep hot food above 60°C and cold food below 5°C.
Clean as you go. Do not leave dirty tools lying around.
Check fridge temperatures daily and write them down.
days.task: Do a food safety check of a kitchen.
days.challenge: Write a food safety checklist for staff.

quiz.q: How often should staff wash hands?
options: Often, especially after touching raw meat
quiz.explain: Hands must be washed often, especially after raw meat or the toilet.

options: So you know food is stored safely
quiz.explain: Daily checks catch a broken fridge before food goes bad.

options: Clean tools and surfaces as you work
quiz.explain: Cleaning as you work keeps the kitchen safe and fast.

days.title: Marketing a Small Restaurant
days.goal: Tell people about your restaurant.

video.title: Your Complete Guide To Restaurant Inventory Management

steps: Take clear photos of your best dishes.
Post your menu and prices on WhatsApp and social media.
Ask happy customers to share your number and photos.
Offer a small discount for a first visit.
Keep a list of regular customers and thank them.
days.task: Post your restaurant menu on WhatsApp or social media.
days.challenge: Ask a happy customer to share your number.

options: Good photos help people decide to visit
quiz.explain: People choose restaurants with their eyes first.

options: Word of mouth is the best free advert
quiz.explain: Happy customers telling friends is the cheapest marketing.

options: Regulars are your most valuable customers
quiz.explain: Regular customers keep a restaurant alive.

days.title: Money: Cash Flow and Profit
days.goal: Understand cash flow and profit in a restaurant.

video.title: An Easy Guide to Restaurant Operations Management

steps: Cash flow is money coming in and going out each day.
Profit is what is left after all costs are paid.
Pay suppliers on time. Late payment can stop your stock.
Keep business money separate from personal money.
Check your numbers weekly: sales, costs, and profit.
days.task: Work out the weekly profit of a small restaurant on paper.
days.challenge: List three ways to cut costs without hurting quality.

options: Money coming in and going out each day
quiz.explain: Cash flow is the daily movement of money in and out.

options: What is left after all costs are paid
quiz.explain: Profit is what remains after you pay for food, staff, rent, and bills.

options: So you always know if the restaurant is making money
quiz.explain: Separate money shows the true health of the business.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Full Restaurant Day
days.goal: Run a full restaurant day from open to close.

video.title: How to Open a Restaurant or Hotel (Step-by-Step) | Complete Business Guide for Beginners 2026

steps: Write the day's plan: menu, staff, and schedule.
Open with your SOP: check stock, prep, and clean.
Serve customers, check back, and handle any complaints.
Count cash, check the POS report, and clean up.
Work out the day's sales, costs, and profit.
days.task: Run a full restaurant day for friends or family as customers.
days.challenge: Write a report on the day: what went well and what to fix.

options: So everyone knows their job and the day runs smoothly
quiz.explain: A day plan keeps the team organised.

quiz.q: What should you do at the end of the day?
options: Count cash, check sales, and clean up
quiz.explain: End-of-day counts and cleaning keep the restaurant healthy.

quiz.q: Why write a report on the day?
options: So you learn and improve next time
quiz.explain: A daily report turns experience into learning.

project.title: Run a Full Restaurant Day
project.brief: Run a restaurant day from open to close with customers.
checks: Day plan written: menu, staff, schedule
Opened with SOP: stock, prep, clean
Customers served and checked on
Complaints handled well, if any
Cash counted and sales checked
Day report written with lessons

days.title: Suppliers: Buy Well
days.goal: Buy from suppliers at good prices.

video.title: How to EASILY Use Restaurant SOPs (Step-by-Step Guide) | DAY 69

steps: A supplier is a person or shop that sells you food and goods.
Get prices from at least three suppliers before you choose.
Buy in bulk for a lower price, but only what you can use before it goes bad.
Check deliveries: count items and check quality.
Pay on time to keep a good relationship.
days.task: Get prices for three items from three suppliers.
days.challenge: Write a delivery checklist: count and quality.

quiz.q: Why get prices from three suppliers?
options: So you find the best price
quiz.explain: Comparing prices stops you paying too much.

options: So you catch short or bad stock at once
quiz.explain: Checking at delivery lets you complain while the driver is there.
On-time payment keeps suppliers happy and your stock flowing.

days.title: Waste: Cut It, Save Money
days.goal: Cut food waste in a restaurant.

video.title: Toast POS System Tutorial for Beginners

steps: Waste is food you throw away. It is money in the bin.
Use FIFO: use old stock first.
Cook to order when you can, so you do not cook too much.
Use leftovers well: soup from vegetables, stock from bones.
Weigh your waste each week and try to cut it.
days.task: Weigh your kitchen waste for a week.
days.challenge: List three ways to cut waste in your kitchen.

options: Food you throw away. It is money in the bin
quiz.explain: Waste is food thrown away. Every bit thrown away is money lost.

options: Use FIFO, cook to order, and reuse leftovers well
quiz.explain: FIFO, cooking to order, and reusing leftovers cut waste.

options: So you can see if waste is going up or down
quiz.explain: Weighing waste shows if your fixes are working.

days.title: Growing: From One Shop to More
days.goal: Grow your restaurant step by step.

video.title: Restaurant — Recipe, Food Cost and Kitchen Stock

steps: Do one restaurant well before you open a second.
Write down your systems: SOPs, menus, and costs.
Train a manager who can run the shop without you.
Save profit to fund growth. Do not borrow too much.
Open a second shop only when the first runs smoothly alone.
days.task: Write a growth plan for your restaurant.
days.challenge: List the systems you would need to copy to a second shop.

quiz.q: When should you open a second restaurant?
options: When the first runs smoothly without you
quiz.explain: A second shop works only when the first runs well on its own.

options: So a new shop can copy what works
quiz.explain: Written systems let you repeat success in a new shop.

options: So the shop runs well when you are away
quiz.explain: A trained manager keeps the shop running without you.

days.title: Your Signature Restaurant
days.goal: Design the restaurant you would love to run.

video.title: Recipe for Restaurant Profits

steps: Pick your concept, your menu, and your prices.
Draw a simple floor plan: kitchen, dining room, and counter.
Write your SOPs for opening and serving.
Work out your start-up costs and daily sales target.
Show the plan to a friend and ask for feedback.
days.task: Design your signature restaurant on paper.
days.challenge: Present it to a friend as if asking for investment.

options: A drawing of the restaurant layout
quiz.explain: A floor plan shows where the kitchen, dining room, and counter go.

options: So you know the space works for staff and customers
quiz.explain: A good layout makes work fast and customers comfortable.

quiz.q: Why present your plan to a friend?
options: Practice helps you explain your idea clearly
quiz.explain: Presenting your plan helps you find gaps in it.

days.title: Keeping Records: Sales, Costs, Profit
days.goal: Keep simple records for your restaurant.

video.title: Restaurant Menu Pricing: How to Increase Profit

steps: Write down daily sales from the POS report.
Write down what you spent on food, staff, and bills.
Work out profit each week.
Note your best-selling dishes and your slowest ones.
Keep all receipts in one place.
days.task: Start a simple record book today, on paper or on your phone.
days.challenge: Work out one week of profit on paper.

options: So you know what you earned each day
quiz.explain: Daily sales records show trends and problems early.

options: So you can prove what you spent
quiz.explain: Receipts prove your costs and help with tax and planning.

quiz.q: Why note best and slowest dishes?
options: So you know what to keep and what to remove
quiz.explain: Sales notes tell you which dishes earn money.

days.title: Restaurant Law and Licences
days.goal: Know the basic rules for running a restaurant.

video.title: Restaurant Menu Pricing Without Guessing

steps: You need a business registration and a food licence in most places.
Your kitchen must pass health checks.
Staff who handle food need health training.
Keep records of your licences and renew them on time.
Ask your local council what rules apply to you.
days.task: Find out what licences a restaurant needs in your area.
days.challenge: Write a list of the licences and their renewal dates.

quiz.q: What licences does a restaurant need?
options: Business registration and a food licence in most places
quiz.explain: Most places need business registration and a food licence.

quiz.q: Why must kitchens pass health checks?
options: So food is safe for customers
quiz.explain: Health checks protect customers from unsafe food.

options: An expired licence can close your restaurant
quiz.explain: An expired licence can get your restaurant shut down.

days.title: Dealing with Slow Days
days.goal: Handle slow days without losing money.

video.title: How to Price Menu Items

steps: Slow days happen. Do not panic.
Offer a lunch deal or a discount to bring people in.
Use slow time to prep, clean, and train staff.
Cook less on slow days so you waste less.
Track which days are slow and plan for them.
days.task: List three things you can do on a slow day.
days.challenge: Plan a lunch deal for a slow day.

quiz.q: What should you do on a slow day?
options: Use the time to prep, clean, and train
quiz.explain: Slow time is good for prep, cleaning, and training.

quiz.q: Why offer a lunch deal on slow days?
quiz.explain: A good deal gives people a reason to visit on a slow day.

options: So you can plan staff and cooking for them
quiz.explain: Knowing your slow days helps you plan and save money.

days.title: Revision: The Manager's Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.

video.title: Your Complete Guide To Restaurant Inventory Management

steps: Work out a food cost percentage from memory.
Price a dish using the food cost method.
Name the parts of a business plan.
Explain FIFO in one sentence.
List your three strongest skills and one to improve.
days.task: Run a small restaurant day from memory, no notes.
days.challenge: Teach one management skill from this course to a friend or family member.

options: Food cost divided by selling price, times 100
quiz.explain: Food cost percentage is food cost divided by selling price, times 100.

options: First in, first out: use old stock first
quiz.explain: FIFO means use the oldest stock first.

quiz.q: Why teach a skill to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Restaurant Launch
days.goal: Plan your capstone restaurant launch.

video.title: An Easy Guide to Restaurant Operations Management

steps: Choose your concept, menu, and prices.
Write your business plan, costs, and sales target.
Write your SOPs for opening, serving, and closing.
Plan your staff schedule for opening week.
Do a trial run of your pop-up if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your pop-up restaurant today.

options: Everything you learned: planning, costing, staff, and service
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why plan staff for opening week?
quiz.explain: A planned schedule stops chaos on opening week.

options: To find problems before the real launch
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Restaurant Launch: Plan, Open and Run Your Small Restaurant
capstone.brief: Launch a small restaurant on paper and in practice: write the business plan, design the menu with prices, cost the dishes, write SOPs, plan staff, and run a pop-up day for real customers. Work out sales, costs, and profit.
